description: The data context templates render with. Templates receive ONLY platform-provided data, never secrets, never other tenants' data. Additive-only within a contract major. Section renderers get {section, brand}; the layout gets {brand, nav, socials}; page templates (pages/{page}.liquid) get their page's documented objects + brand.

variables.description: The one content tree (content model v1, contract/v1/content-model.json): site.brand, site.nav, site.socials, site.locale and the typed collections under site.content.*. Available to every render scope; page templates receive it alongside their page objects.
The organisation's branding (same shape as the flat-era brand object).
Navigation: items (curated main or platform-derived), footer, derived, the flat-era nav shape, re-addressed.
Social links, the flat-era socials shape.
Locale: code, direction, languages.

The typed collections: services, events, articles, campaigns, causes, courses, resources, locations, schedules, about. EVERY collection is bounded (cap + moreHref in the model registry), every enum is open, every optional field explicitly nullable, and the model only ever grows. The validator computes your template's content footprint from the paths you read and stamps the required minimum model version at publish; dynamic indexing into site.content is refused so the footprint stays decidable.
The typed content of the section being rendered, its shape is the section type's fields (see the section catalogue).
The charity's display name.
The charity's tagline.
The charity's logo URL, or null when none is set, always branch on it.
'full' (the image already contains the name, show it alone) or 'icon' (a mark, show it beside brand.name).

Optional FOOTER mark (often a lighter or single-colour logo variant the tenant uploads for dark footers), or null, always branch. When unset, fall back to your own choice: the main logo, or the name as text.

The site's primary navigation. By default platform-derived per tenant (pages that exist, features that are on); when the tenant has curated a header menu, this IS that menu instead, the same { label, href, cta?, external?, children? } shape either way, so render ALL of it exactly as before.
The item's display label (tenant-chosen for some items, treat as text, it is escaped like everything else).
The item's destination path.
True for the call-to-action item (Donate), style it prominently.
Optional sub-items for dropdowns and mega menus. Children use the same item shape and may carry one further children level, giving a maximum of two levels below the top item.
True when the item points off-site (a tenant-curated external link), add target="_blank" rel="noopener". Absent/false for internal links.
Optional tenant-authored column or topic label for grouping items inside a mega menu.
Optional short supporting text for a richer navigation card.
Optional image URL for a navigation card. Always branch when absent.

Optional mega-menu presentation metadata on a top-level item: columns (2 to 4) and an optional promo object with title, text, href, label and imageUrl. It is content only; the template owns hover, focus and responsive presentation in CSS.

The tenant's curated FOOTER menu, the same item shape as nav.items[] (label, href, cta?, external?, children?). EMPTY when the tenant hasn't built one, so branch on nav.footer.size before rendering a footer-menu block (derive or omit). Optional to support, a template that ignores it simply shows its own footer.

The platform's AUTOMATIC nav (same item shape as nav.items[]), always present even when the tenant has curated nav.items. Use it when you want the auto, feature-aware list somewhere regardless of the tenant's header curation; most templates just render nav.items.
The tenant's configured social links (possibly empty). Render icons via iconSvg, platform-generated markup, safe for the raw filter (the one exception beyond richtext fields).
Platform key (facebook, instagram, x, …).
The profile URL.
The platform-drawn icon SVG for this network, output with | raw.

The tenant's worship-schedule rail (prayer/service times), or null when not configured, ALWAYS branch on it. Faith-neutral: every label is tenant data. Render it as header chrome (the reference pattern is a utility bar above the nav); omit entirely when null. Rendering it requires declaring supports.worship in the manifest (the validator checks both directions), the choosers use that declaration to steer worship-enabled tenants.
Up to 8 rows of {name, begins, congregation}, name is the prayer/service name; begins and congregation are display strings (times or short text), either may be null.
Row label for the begins times (tenant-set; defaults to 'Begins').
Row label for the congregation times (tenant-set; e.g. "Jama'at"; defaults to 'Congregation'). Only meaningful when at least one row carries a congregation value.
A short free-text line for the rail (e.g. "Jum'a 13:15 & 14:15"), or null.
A same-site path the note links to (a service page with full timetables), or null.
Today's date, platform-formatted (e.g. "24 July 2026").
Today in the tenant's alternate calendar (Islamic civil calendar, e.g. "11 Safar 1448") when they opted in, else null, always branch.

The next prayer or service as {name, begins, congregation, target}, or null. target is an ISO timestamp in the organisation's timezone. Templates may display it statically; use the next_prayer island for a ticking countdown.
Structured Friday congregations as rows of {name, begins, congregation}. Empty for schedules without configured Friday times.
Structured alternate-calendar data. Contract v1 exposes {display}, or null when disabled.
Upcoming structured observances as {name, date, href}. Empty until the tenant has authored observances.
The public rendering locale and direction. Always present as {code, direction, languages}.
Current BCP 47 language code, currently en, cy or ar.
ltr or rtl. The platform also applies this direction to the document element.
Supported public languages as {code, label, direction}. Place the language_switch island for platform-owned switching behaviour.

The tenant's published events, soonest first, a CURATED read-only view for display. On page:events it is every published event; on section:events it is the TICKETED ones (the section's purpose). Transactional steps (RSVP, ticket purchase) stay platform-owned on the detail view, link with detailHref, never rebuild those flows.
Published and currently available appeals. This is a display-only summary; payment processor identifiers and transaction configuration are never exposed. Empty when there is no active appeal.

An appeal card with id, title, slug, description, imageUrl, targetAmount, raisedAmount, progressPercentage, href and a boolean paymentOptions summary. Always use href to reach the platform donation flow.
Published services and programmes in display order. Empty when none are published, so omit the section rather than inventing cards.
A service card with id, title, slug, summary, imageUrl and href. Use href rather than constructing a route.
Public documents from the tenant's media library, newest first. Private assets are never included. Empty when no public documents exist.
A safe document link with id, title, folder, url, contentType, bytes and publishedAt. Always use url rather than constructing storage paths.
Public locations from the tenant's venue book, primary first. Empty when no venues are configured.
A public location with id, name, address, latitude, longitude, primary and directionsHref. Provider references and private notes are excluded.

The tenant's INFO events (special days, no sign-up, no payment), soonest first. The same curated event shape as events[]. Render them your way, or place {% island 'whats_on_strip' %} for the ready-made strip. Empty when none, render nothing you invent (derive or omit).
The newest published articles (up to 6), newest first. Render them your way, or place {% island 'latest_articles' %} for the ready-made strip. Empty when none, derive or omit.
The article's title.
The canonical link to the article, always use this.
Short summary, or null, branch on it.
Cover image URL, or null, always branch.
ISO-8601 publish time, or null, format with the date filter.
Estimated reading minutes, or null.
The article's category names (possibly empty), treat as text.
The tenant's live campaigns, in display order. Empty when none are live, render nothing.
The campaign's name.
The canonical link to the campaign page, always use this.
Short summary, or null, branch on it.
Featured image URL, or null, always branch.
What the tenant calls their campaigns section ("Campaigns" by default), the heading fallback.

Published article summaries for the current listing or selected category. Each item contains id, title, slug, excerpt, imageUrl, authorName, authorRole, categories, publishedAt, readingMinutes, engagement counts and href.
The active category filter, or null on an unfiltered listing.

The article detail being displayed. It carries the article summary fields plus sanitised bodyHtml, updatedAt and allowComments. Render bodyHtml with the raw filter; engagement and comments remain platform islands.
Up to three other published article summaries, newest first.
Categories currently used by published articles. Each item has name, count and href.
Stable event id.
The event's name.
Plain-text description, or null, branch on it.
INFO (no sign-up), RSVP (free sign-up) or TICKETED (paid).
ISO-8601 start, format with the date filter.
ISO-8601 end, or null.
Venue name, or null (online events may have none).
True for online events.
Promo image URL, or null, always branch.
False before sales open.
True when no capacity remains.
The cheapest ticket price (number), or null for free/INFO events.
ISO currency code for priceFrom, or null.
The canonical link to this event's detail view, always use this, never build URLs yourself.
The course this page addresses, a CURATED read-only view for display. The enrolment journey itself is the platform-owned course_enrol island; place it, never rebuild it.
Stable course id.
The course's title.
Plain-text summary, or null, branch on it. Prefer aboutHtml for the body when present.
The tenant-authored About page as SANITISED HTML (platform-sanitised on save; images resolved), render with the raw filter inside your prose styles, or null when not written.
The MAIN image (hero) URL, or null, always branch.
Venue display text, or null.
EVERYONE, or CHILD for children-only courses (parents enrol their children).
UPFRONT (one payment), TERM (committed term fee), or ROLLING (monthly with notice).
ISO date the term starts, or null, format with the date filter.
ISO date the term ends, or null.
ISO currency code for priceFrom.
The cheapest priced option (number), or null when every option is free.
True when no option has places left (the island shows the standard note).
The canonical link back to the courses listing, always use this.

course.description: Weekly athletics for children aged 7 to 12, coached by qualified volunteers at the King's Park track.
course.aboutHtml:
What we do

Track and field fundamentals in a friendly, coached setting: warm-ups, drills, and a different discipline every week.

  • Sprints, relays and middle distance
  • Long jump, high jump and throws
  • A club mini-meet at the end of every term

What to bring

Trainers, a water bottle and a waterproof. Everything else, including spikes for the older group, is provided.

article.title: The Community Garden Opens Its Gates
article.excerpt: Two years of digging, fundraising and Saturday mornings in the rain: the Foundry Lane garden is finally open to everyone.
article.bodyHtml:
A shared place to grow

The gates opened at ten. By half past, every raised bed had a family around it, the tool shed had a queue, and somebody had already claimed the sunny corner by the wall for tomatoes.

The Foundry Lane garden has been two years in the making. It began as a patch of rubble behind the old ironworks, offered to us on a peppercorn lease after the Winter Fair of 2028, and it has been built almost entirely by volunteer weekends since: twenty-two raised beds, a wheelchair-accessible path, a rainwater store, and a greenhouse pieced together from three donated ones.

I have lived on this street forty years and never once stood on this ground. Now my grandchildren grow beans here.

What happens next

The beds are allocated, but the garden is not finished, and it is not meant to be. This season the growers' committee has three priorities:

  • A covered seating area, so the garden works in the rain it will certainly get
  • Weekly sessions with the youth club, growing the salads the kitchen crew cook with
  • A seed library in the old gatehouse, free to any Alderford household

If you can lay a slab, mend a frame or simply keep a kettle going, the volunteer team would love to hear from you. And if you just want somewhere green to sit, the gate is open every day until dusk.

Thank you

To the eighty-one people who gave to the garden appeal, the six local firms who lent tools and time, and the council officers who said yes when it mattered: this one is yours as much as ours.
